<div class="comment-body markdown-body js-comment-body soft-wrap user-select-contain d-block">

This updates the github actions cataloger to consider cases when there are explicit version annotations added to pinned action references. So without this change:

<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" snippet-clipboard-copy-content="jobs:
  static-analysis:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683 #v4.2.2">

``` notranslate
jobs:
  static-analysis:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683 #v4.2.2
```

</div>

... syft would pick up on this package as `actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683`, however with this PR now it will be raised up as `actions/checkout@v4.2.2` with additional metadata exposing the original values:

<div class="highlight highlight-source-go notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" snippet-clipboard-copy-content="Metadata: pkg.GitHubActionsUseStatement{
    Value:   &quot;actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683&quot;,
    Comment: &quot;v4.2.2&quot;,
},">

``` notranslate
Metadata: pkg.GitHubActionsUseStatement{
    Value:   "actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683",
    Comment: "v4.2.2",
},
```

<div class="comment-body markdown-body js-comment-body soft-wrap user-select-contain d-block css-overflow-wrap-anywhere">

It felt necessary since we're parsing a comment and treating it as the source of truth for a package version. The original version is lost without having a metadata type that exposes this.

> If Syft hasn't parsed a version or a sha, it's unlikely this is of use to anyone else, is it?

this resonates in the sense that if there is no comment to parse this is a useless metadata object.

> I wonder if there would be utility in allowing different "levels" of detail in the SBOM.

Do you have an example or idea how this would work?

I don't really have an example but I would think something like logging levels but for SBOM detail. Maybe we determine level=1 is NTIA minimum elements, and level=2, 3, etc.. add more details up to including parsed data like full MANFIEST.MF and Portable Executable properties, etc.. where the lowest level excludes these details. There probably isn't a reason to do this, just an idle thought. This all was me thinking about SBOM size that some people may at some point be concerned with this.
